editorial.titleTr: China's Semiconductor Rise Triggers Market Plunge, Time to Share Windfall Profits?
summaryTr: Chinese semiconductor companies are making waves in the global market through listings and technological self-reliance.
South Korean firms such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix must brace for China's growth.
Maintaining technological superiority and expanding the ecosystem have become key survival strategies.
editorial.bodyTr: Chinese semiconductor companies are making major waves in the global semiconductor market through stock market listings, technological self-sufficiency in semiconductors, and strengthened competitiveness in AI models. Korean semiconductor firms such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix must remain vigilant about China's growth and investment, and the importance of maintaining technological superiority and expanding ecosystem strategies has become even more critical.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Last-Minute 'Dismissal of Charges' Clause—Whose Interests Does It Serve?
summaryTr: The Democratic Party added vague grounds for dismissing prosecutions to the Criminal Procedure Act.
This is criticized as an attempt by President Lee Jae-myung to resolve his judicial risks.
Court pressure and the composition of the judiciary have become central to political conflict.
editorial.bodyTr: The Democratic Party is drawing controversy by adding vague grounds for dismissing indictments, such as "serious illegal investigations," to a criminal procedure law amendment. The move faces criticism for being an attempt to pressure the courts to resolve President Lee Jae-myung's judicial risks, and is emerging as a central issue in political conflict as it becomes intertwined with the future composition of the judiciary, including the appointment of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

summaryTr: KOSPI's historic July plunge spreads market panic

summaryTr: The Army's First Corps was made to stand guard at the front lines without live ammunition.

editorial.body: 입력 최전방 부대에 설치된 K6 중기관총. 중앙포토 서부전선을 관할하는 육군 1군단의 최전방 소초(GP)와 일반전초(GOP)에서 올해 상반기부터 K6 중기관총에 실탄을 장전하지 않은 채 경계작전을 해 왔던 것으로 나타났다. 군사분계선(MDL)과 인접한 GP와 GOP는 북한군이 침투하거나 군사 도발을 감행했을 때 초를 다투며 즉각 응전해야 하는 곳이다. 특히 분당 600발의 12.7㎜ 실탄 발사 능력을 갖춘 K6 중기관총은 핵심 공용화기다. 실탄을 장착하고 언제든 사격이 가능하도록 유지토록 한 것도 이 때문이다. 그런데 수도권 전방을 방어하는 부대에서 탄약을 기관총과 아예 분리해 탄통에 넣은 뒤 총기 옆에 두도록 지침을 바꿨다고 하니 1군단에선 사실상 ‘빈총 경계’를 해 온 셈이다. 이 기간 북한의 도발이 없었던 것이 천만다행일 따름이다. 더 큰 문제는 군 작전을 총괄하는 합동참모본부의 뒷북 대응이다. 합참은 언론 취재가 시작되자 “현장 확인 후 필요한 조치를 하겠다”고 밝혔다. 최전방 경계 태세의 허점을 자인한 것은 물론, 군의 지휘 및 보고 체계가 먹통이었음을 드러낸 것이다. 1군단이 기존 지침을 변경한 정확한 이유는 확인되지 않았다. 다만 그동안 K6 중기관총의 점검 과정에서 간혹 오발 사고가 발생했던 만큼 이를 막기 위한 관리 차원일 수 있다. 만약 지휘관의 책임을 피하기 위한 편의주의적 발상이었거나 긴장 완화라는 명목을 고려한 조치였다면 안보의 본말이 뒤바뀐, 군의 본분을 망각한 조치라는 지적을 피하기 어렵다. 총기사고가 두려워 실탄을 빼놓는다면 그것은 ‘싸우는 군대’가 아니라 우리 군이 ‘사고 예방만 고려하는 관리형 군대’로 전락했음을 의미한다. 지금 최전방의 안보 환경은 어느 때보다 엄중하다. 북한은 MDL 일대에 지뢰를 매설하고 철조망을 설치하는가 하면, 자주포 진지까지 전진 배치하며 위협 수위를 높이고 있다. 북한군이 정면으로 안보를 위협하고 있는 상황에서 최소한의 자위적 대응 조치마저 포기하고, 이를 군 지휘부가 인지하지 못한 현실은 군 기강 해이라고밖에 볼 수 없다. 군 당국은 1군단의 지침 변경 경위를 철저히 조사해 재발 방지 태책을 마련해야 한다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Firing Blanks at the Front-Line Posts
summaryTr: Troops at a forward outpost on the western front conducted guard operations without loading live ammunition into their K6 medium machine gun.
It was revealed that 'empty gun watch' was being conducted at a location where immediate counterfire should be mounted in response to North Korean provocation.
The Joint Chiefs of Staff's belated response and the collapse of the military command reporting system represent serious discipline breakdown.
editorial.bodyTr: K6 medium machine guns installed at frontline positions. Frontline observation posts (GPs) and general outposts (GOPs) under Army First Corps, which oversees the western front, have been conducting guard operations without live ammunition loaded into K6 medium machine guns since the first half of this year. GPs and GOPs adjacent to the Military Demarcation Line must respond immediately in seconds if North Korean troops attempt infiltration or launch military provocations. The K6 medium machine gun, equipped with the capability to fire 1,200 rounds per minute of 12.7mm live ammunition, is a critical shared weapon system. This is precisely why it was maintained with ammunition loaded and ready to fire at any moment. However, the unit defending the capital area changed its guidelines to separate ammunition from the machine guns, store it in ammunition boxes, and place it beside the guns. This means First Corps has essentially been conducting "empty gun watch." It is fortunate that North Korea refrained from provocation during this period. A more serious problem is the delayed response from the Joint Chiefs of Staff, which oversees all military operations. When media inquiries began, the Joint Chiefs stated they would "take necessary measures after confirming the situation on the ground." This amounts to acknowledging gaps in frontline security posture and revealing that the military's command and reporting system has broken down. The exact reason First Corps changed its existing guidelines has not been confirmed. It is possible, however, that the decision was made for safety management purposes, given that accidental discharges occasionally occurred during K6 medium machine gun inspections. If the measure was motivated by a desire to avoid command responsibility or represented a convenience-driven approach or a move toward reduced tensions, it cannot escape criticism as a reversal of security priorities and a dereliction of military duty. If live ammunition is removed due to fears of gun accidents, it means our military has not become a "fighting military" but rather has devolved into a "management-focused military" concerned only with accident prevention. The security environment at the frontlines is graver than ever. North Korea is laying mines and installing barbed wire along the MDL, while deploying self-propelled artillery positions forward and escalating threats. In a situation where North Korean forces are directly threatening security, abandoning even minimal measures of self-defense and the military leadership's failure to recognize this can only be seen as military discipline deterioration. Military authorities must thoroughly investigate the circumstances behind First Corps' change in guidelines and establish measures to prevent recurrence.

editorial.title: Broken ladder
editorial.body: Blanket property lending restrictions widen South Korea's generational wealth divide Every society tells itself a story about how prosperity is earned. In South Korea, that story has long centered on one milestone: buying a first home. As that milestone drifts further out of reach, the country's housing problem becomes more than expensive apartments; it becomes a question of whether work still offers a credible route to building wealth. According to newly released government data, only 27.7 percent of household heads aged 39 and younger owned the home they lived in as of March 2025, the lowest level since comparable statistics began in 2017. The decline has continued for six straight years. By contrast, homeownership among people in their 50s stood at 63.5 percent and among those aged 60 or older at 68.5 percent. The gap between the youngest and oldest generations has widened to a record 40.8 percentage points. These figures capture more than a difficult housing market. They show that asset ownership is becoming increasingly concentrated across generations. Home prices have risen far faster than wages. Seoul's average apartment price has climbed to nearly 1.58 billion won ($1.08 million), while the price-to-income ratio has reached roughly 10.5 years of a middle-income household's total earnings before living expenses. For young workers facing an uncertain labor market, the real saving period would be considerably longer. Homeownership increasingly depends on wealth or access to credit. That is why blanket lending restrictions warrant reconsideration. Korea must guard against excessive household debt and speculative borrowing. Yet policies aimed at cooling the market affect buyers very differently. Wealthy households with abundant cash can continue purchasing property despite tighter mortgage ceilings. First-time buyers with stable incomes but limited savings cannot. Recent cases in which commercial banks exhausted mortgage quotas within minutes for newly completed apartment complexes illustrate how indiscriminate credit controls can trap owner-occupiers rather than speculators. Housing has long been Korea's principal means of household wealth accumulation. When younger families lose access to that first step, the wealth gap widens. Homeownership among households in the lowest wealth quintile is just 6.8 percent, compared with 84.2 percent in the highest. The result is a society where wealth increasingly reflects existing assets rather than productive work, making upward mobility progressively more elusive. The disconnect becomes even clearer in the broader economy. Korea continues to attract enormous investment in semiconductors and artificial intelligence, with new international partnerships promising future growth. Those developments are welcome. Yet capital-intensive industries employ only a small share of the workforce. For many young workers confronting stagnant purchasing power and an inaccessible housing market, record investment announcements offer little immediate reassurance. Economic success loses some of its meaning when participation in the country's largest source of wealth creation remains beyond reach. The national real estate forum chaired by President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday demonstrated that policymakers recognize the depth of public frustration. The debate focused on taxes, lending and housing supply. Raising holding taxes on speculative ownership may merit consideration, particularly if owner-occupiers are distinguished from investors. Yet taxes alone cannot repair a housing ladder that has already lost several rungs. Nor should broad credit restraints become a substitute for more careful regulation. Prudential oversight should remain firm while lending rules distinguish speculative investors from creditworthy first-time buyers. Governments must also deliver credible plans to expand housing supply where demand is strongest. Financial stability remains essential. Preventing housing bubbles is equally important. But stability should not come at the cost of permanently excluding the generation expected to sustain the economy. Housing policy succeeds not when it suppresses borrowing for everyone, but when it distinguishes speculation from aspiration. After all, a functioning market is one where productive work, prudent borrowing and responsible regulation still arrive at the same destination: a realistic chance to own a first home. 일괄적인 대출 제한은 첫 주택 구입자들에게 타격을 주는 반면 현금이 풍부한 구매자들은 영향을 받지 않아 실수요자들을 함정에 빠뜨리고 있다.
정책 입안자들은 투기 목적의 투자자와 신용도 있는 구매자를 구분하고 주택 공급을 확대해 상향 이동성을 회복해야 한다.

주택소유는 점점 더 기존 부에 접근성에 달려 있다. 바로 이 때문에 포괄적 대출 규제는 재검토할 필요가 있다. 한국은 과도한 가계 부채와 투기적 차입을 경계해야 한다. 그러나 시장을 진정시키기 위한 정책들은 구매자들에게 매우 다르게 영향을 미친다. 풍부한 현금을 보유한 부유한 가구는 더 엄격한 주택담보대출 한도에도 불구하고 계속 부동산을 구입할 수 있다. 안정적인 소득을 가졌지만 저축이 적은 첫 주택 구매자는 그럴 수 없다. 최근 상업은행들이 새로 완공된 아파트 단지에 대한 주택담보대출 한도를 몇 분 내에 소진한 사례들은 무분별한 신용 규제가 투기꾼보다는 자주택 구매자를 어떻게 함정에 빠뜨릴 수 있는지를 보여준다.

주택은 오랫동안 한국의 가구 자산 축적의 주요 수단이었다. 젊은 가족들이 그 첫 단계에 대한 접근을 잃을 때, 부의 격차는 더욱 벌어진다. 가장 낮은 부의 5분위수에 속하는 가구의 주택소유율은 6.8퍼센트에 불과한 반면, 가장 높은 5분위수에서는 84.2퍼센트다. 그 결과는 부가 생산적 노동보다는 기존 자산을 반영하는 사회이며, 상향 이동성은 점점 더 어려워진다.

이러한 단절은 더 넓은 경제에서도 더욱 명확해진다. 한국은 반도체와 인공지능에 막대한 투자를 계속 유치하고 있으며, 새로운 국제 파트너십들은 향후 성장을 약속하고 있다. 이러한 발전은 환영할 만하다. 그럼에도 자본집약적 산업들은 노동력의 일부만 고용한다. 정체된 구매력과 접근 불가능한 주택 시장에 직면한 많은 젊은 근로자들에게, 기록적인 투자 발표는 즉각적인 안심을 거의 제공하지 못한다. 경제적 성공은 국가의 가장 큰 부의 창출원에 대한 참여가 여전히 범위를 벗어날 때 일부 의미를 잃는다.

editorials.title: Broken ladder
editorials.body: Blanket property lending restrictions widen South Korea's generational wealth divide Every society tells itself a story about how prosperity is earned. In South Korea, that story has long centered on one milestone: buying a first home. As that milestone drifts further out of reach, the country's housing problem becomes more than expensive apartments; it becomes a question of whether work still offers a credible route to building wealth. According to newly released government data, only 27.7 percent of household heads aged 39 and younger owned the home they lived in as of March 2025, the lowest level since comparable statistics began in 2017. The decline has continued for six straight years. By contrast, homeownership among people in their 50s stood at 63.5 percent and among those aged 60 or older at 68.5 percent. The gap between the youngest and oldest generations has widened to a record 40.8 percentage points. These figures capture more than a difficult housing market. They show that asset ownership is becoming increasingly concentrated across generations. Home prices have risen far faster than wages. Seoul's average apartment price has climbed to nearly 1.58 billion won ($1.08 million), while the price-to-income ratio has reached roughly 10.5 years of a middle-income household's total earnings before living expenses. For young workers facing an uncertain labor market, the real saving period would be considerably longer. Homeownership increasingly depends on wealth or access to credit. That is why blanket lending restrictions warrant reconsideration. Korea must guard against excessive household debt and speculative borrowing. Yet policies aimed at cooling the market affect buyers very differently. Wealthy households with abundant cash can continue purchasing property despite tighter mortgage ceilings. First-time buyers with stable incomes but limited savings cannot. Recent cases in which commercial banks exhausted mortgage quotas within minutes for newly completed apartment complexes illustrate how indiscriminate credit controls can trap owner-occupiers rather than speculators. Housing has long been Korea's principal means of household wealth accumulation. When younger families lose access to that first step, the wealth gap widens. Homeownership among households in the lowest wealth quintile is just 6.8 percent, compared with 84.2 percent in the highest. The result is a society where wealth increasingly reflects existing assets rather than productive work, making upward mobility progressively more elusive. The disconnect becomes even clearer in the broader economy. Korea continues to attract enormous investment in semiconductors and artificial intelligence, with new international partnerships promising future growth. Those developments are welcome. Yet capital-intensive industries employ only a small share of the workforce. For many young workers confronting stagnant purchasing power and an inaccessible housing market, record investment announcements offer little immediate reassurance. Economic success loses some of its meaning when participation in the country's largest source of wealth creation remains beyond reach. The national real estate forum chaired by President Lee Jae Myung on Thursday demonstrated that policymakers recognize the depth of public frustration. The debate focused on taxes, lending and housing supply. Raising holding taxes on speculative ownership may merit consideration, particularly if owner-occupiers are distinguished from investors. Yet taxes alone cannot repair a housing ladder that has already lost several rungs. Nor should broad credit restraints become a substitute for more careful regulation. Prudential oversight should remain firm while lending rules distinguish speculative investors from creditworthy first-time buyers. Governments must also deliver credible plans to expand housing supply where demand is strongest. Financial stability remains essential. Preventing housing bubbles is equally important. But stability should not come at the cost of permanently excluding the generation expected to sustain the economy. Housing policy succeeds not when it suppresses borrowing for everyone, but when it distinguishes speculation from aspiration. After all, a functioning market is one where productive work, prudent borrowing and responsible regulation still arrive at the same destination: a realistic chance to own a first home. 금융 안정성은 여전히 필수적이다. 주택 거품을 방지하는 것 역시 마찬가지로 중요하다. 하지만 안정성이 경제를 지탱하기로 예상되는 세대를 영구적으로 배제하는 대가로 이루어져서는 안 된다. 주택 정책은 모두를 위해 차입을 억제할 때가 아니라 투기와 열망을 구분할 때 성공한다. 결국 제대로 작동하는 시장이란 생산적 노동, 신중한 차입, 그리고 책임감 있는 규제가 여전히 같은 목적지에 도달하는 시장이다. 바로 첫 주택을 소유할 실질적인 기회다.

editorials.titleTr: Median Income Benchmark Rises 6% for Fourth Consecutive Year as Welfare Burden Surges
summaryTr: The standard median income rose 6.7 percent next year, marking four consecutive years of increases in the 6 percent range.

editorials.bodyTr: The government's standard median income, which serves as the benchmark for welfare programs, will increase by 6.7 percent next year.
